== Biography ==
Jane was born about 1799. She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-1657|John Glasgow]] and [[McClure-6341|Jane McClure]].  She passed away in 1837.
== Research Notes ==

=== The Armstrong nephew ===
The diary of [[Glasgow-1780|James McClure Glasgow]] names Rev. James Glasgow Armstrong of St Louis as his nephew on 24 April 1870. The minister is identified with the 1836 Belfast-born husband of Alma Emily Hitchcock in the Hitchcock genealogy,p. 95.<ref>[https://presbyterianhistoryireland.com/publications/heritage/ John Faris, “A Black Sheep,” Heritage, Autumn 2023, diary extract 24 April 1870]; [https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/15/The_genealogy_of_the_Hitchcock_family%2C_who_are_descended_from_Matthias_Hitchcock_of_East_Haven%2C_Conn.%2C_and_Luke_Hitchcock_of_Wethersfield%2C_Conn_%28IA_cu31924012053785%29.pdf The genealogy of the Hitchcock family,p. 95]. Published transcriptions and searchable genealogy; original diary and genealogy page image uninspected.</ref>
[[Glasgow-1779|Jane Glasgow Armstrong]] is the preferred probable mother, 72% subjective confidence, because she is the missionary’s documented Armstrong sister and her generation fits. No source inspected names her as mother. The separate 1838 Anne Armstrong case, whose mother was Jane Glasgow, remains a competing route; no identity merge or Armstrong father is inferred.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050122635/ Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser,27 July 1838,p. 3, Antrim Assizes]. Held source account; Anne’s birth surname and family identity unproved.</ref>
